target.body:
Related: #103281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where container upgrades could remain unhealthy when startup migrations encountered recoverable legacy Codex session metadata and Memory Core index conflicts. The gateway would repeatedly refuse readiness even though the Codex sidecars had no possible session owner and the canonical Memory Core index was already authoritative.

## Why This Change Was Made

Codex ownership discovery now ignores metadata-only session rows that have no transcript identity, while retaining fail-closed validation for rows that claim a session ID. Memory Core now treats only a legacy `files` row conflict as a derived-index convergence case: it keeps the canonical per-agent SQLite rows and archives the obsolete sidecar. Other malformed, ambiguous, vector, FTS, metadata, and reference conflicts remain untouched for review.

## User Impact

Affected upgrades can complete during normal gateway startup without a separate `openclaw doctor --fix` container. Existing canonical session and memory data remains authoritative, and genuinely indeterminate migration state still blocks readiness instead of being discarded.

## Evidence

- Regressions reproduced the current-main blockers before the fix: a metadata-only session row caused `session index ... has invalid entries`, and conflicting legacy Memory Core `files` rows prevented archival.
- Rebased-head focused plugin contract suites: 51 tests passed (`23` Codex, `28` Memory Core) on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx8tzebxmewt0db5a9msxxxn`.
- `pnpm check:changed` passed on Blacksmith Testbox, including extension production/test typechecks, lint, database-first storage guard, runtime-sidecar-loader guard, and import-cycle check.

target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow only enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting. The three `fetch` calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request `AbortSignal` timeout, so a stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response could bypass that deadline and leave the CLI spinner stuck. A server that returned headers and then stalled the body could also escape an incomplete timeout catch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under the same `AbortSignal.timeout` (30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry on per-operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — one operation deadline for fetch + body read on user-code, poll, and token-exchange; poll retries on timeout within the 15-minute deadline
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code aborts with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - hung token exchange aborts with timeout error
  - success path asserts all three fetches carry an `AbortSignal`
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall: user-code / token-exchange abort with formatted timeout; poll retries and succeeds

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI Codex device-code login no longer leaves individual HTTP operations unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return, or returns headers and then stalls the body.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs device-code auth → `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `requestOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `exchangeOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `runOpenAICodexDeviceCodeRequest` (`fetch` + `readOpenAICodexDeviceBody` under `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production device-code helpers exercised via colocated Vitest against a real hanging `node:http` loopback that sends headers then a partial JSON prefix and never finishes the body. Only `AbortSignal.timeout` duration is shortened for deterministic proof; the production fetch+body composition and error/retry mapping stay unmocked.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Matches the existing 30s OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth token request timeout; uses `AbortSignal.timeout` like GitHub Copilot device-flow request timeouts. Does not migrate this path onto `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in this change.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, product checkout on branch `fix/openai-device-code-request-timeout`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```

 ✓ aborts hung token exchange requests instead of waiting forever 0ms

 ✓ aborts when token-exchange headers arrive but the body never completes 43ms

      Tests  14 passed (14)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.53s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Hung user-code and token-exchange fetches abort with `OpenAI device code ... timed out after 30000ms`; a poll `TimeoutError` (including post-header body stall) is retried and the login can still succeed within the overall deadline. Real loopback partial-body stalls exercise production body consumption under the same operation signal.
- **What was not tested:** Live `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code` against a real stalled `auth.openai.com` endpoint.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

target.title: fix(gateway): stop health monitor from undoing crash-loop give-up
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the gateway channel health monitor could erase a channel manager's crash-loop restart progress and revive accounts after the manager had already given up. Operators configuring permanent give-up after repeated channel start failures would see the account keep restarting instead of staying stopped.

Closes #104458

## Why This Change Was Made

The manager already owns crash-loop accounting (backoff and terminal give-up). This change makes that ownership an explicit closed contract (`resolveHealthRecoveryOwnership` / `resolveChannelHealthRecoveryOwnership`) and teaches the health monitor to skip stop/start/reset when the manager already owns recovery. Timed-out recovery (restartPending with zero attempts) remains monitor-available so wedged-task recovery is preserved.

## User Impact

Failing channel accounts that hit the manager's restart budget stay given-up instead of being silently revived. Mid-backoff accounts keep their consecutive-attempt counter, so give-up remains a stable terminal state under the default health monitor.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Focused tests (pass):
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts \
  src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts
# Test Files  12 passed (12)  Tests  316 passed (316)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)  Tests  96 passed (96)
```

Static closeout (after `pnpm check:changed` stuck on local install thrash):
```text
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD  # exit 0
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.ts \
  src/gateway/channel-health-policy.ts src/gateway/server-channels.ts
# Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Health monitor must not clear manager `restartAttempts` during mid-backoff, and must not `startChannel` after manager give-up. **Also:** after a prior crash-loop attempt, a recovery stop timeout must remain monitor-owned so the follow-up `startChannel` can replace the timed-out task (CS P1).
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, monitor only treated `restartPending && reconnectAttempts===0` as continuing recovery, so mid-backoff (`reconnectAttempts>0`) and gave-up (`reconnectAttempts>=10`, not pending) still called `resetRestartAttempts` + `startChannel`. Existing test even expected give-up revival. PR head also misclassified stop-timeout recovery as manager `active-backoff` when the attempt map still held a prior count.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts -t "does not clear attempts or revive a channel after manager give-up"`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts -t "does not clear manager crash-loop progress during mid-backoff"`
  3. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts -t "resolveChannelHealthRecoveryOwnership"`
  4. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts -t "keeps timeout recovery available after prior crash-loop attempts"`
  5. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts -t "composed manager+monitor: timeout recovery still restarts after prior crash-loop attempts"`
  6. Full focused suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts`
- Evidence after fix (deterministic manager+monitor lifecycle):
  ```text
  # Timeout-recovery ownership + composed monitor restart (after CS P1 fix)
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts \
    -t "keeps timeout recovery available|composed manager"
  # Test Files  1 passed (1)
  # Tests  2 passed | 48 skipped (50)

  # Full focused surface
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-channels.test.ts \
    src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts \
    src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts \
    src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts
  # Test Files  14 passed (14)
  # Tests  416 passed (416)
  ```
  Lifecycle sequence covered by the new composed case:
  1. First start fails → manager crash-loop attempt counter becomes > 0
  2. Second start hangs while running with retained reconnectAttempts
  3. Non-manual stop times out → `recoveryStopTimedOut` + `restartPending`, snapshot `reconnectAttempts=0`
  4. `resolveHealthRecoveryOwnership` returns `{ kind: "available" }` (not `active-backoff`)
  5. Health monitor arms recovery then starts a replacement task; channel returns to `running: true`
- Control check: Sibling monitor cases still restart stuck/disconnected/ordinary-stopped accounts; give-up and mid-backoff still skip `resetRestartAttempts`/`startChannel`; continuing pending recovery with `reconnectAttempts=0` still bypasses cooldown.
- Observed result after fix: Manager-owned recovery phases are skipped by the monitor; attempt counter and terminal give-up are preserved; timed-out stop recovery after prior attempts is still monitor-owned and restarts.
- What was not tested: Multi-hour simulated default-timing harness from the issue report; live provider channel crash loops.

target.title: fix(telegram): prevent unlisted API calls from stalling delivery
target.body:
Closes #104524

AI-assisted: yes. I used an OpenAI coding agent, reviewed the resulting change, and understand the timeout behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users could have all outbound replies for a session stall for roughly eight minutes when an API call used a method that was not explicitly listed in the client timeout table.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every identified Telegram API method except `getUpdates` now receives the existing 60-second outbound timeout as a default. Explicit method-specific guards remain unchanged, higher configured timeouts are still honored, and requests whose method cannot be identified remain untouched.

## User Impact

A newly introduced or otherwise unlisted Telegram API method can no longer silently fall back to grammY's approximately 500-second timeout and park the serialized delivery lane. Its client-side guard defaults to 60 seconds unless the operator configured a higher timeout.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 1 file, 15 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — 142 files, 2,666 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.

- `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=2300' node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/telegram/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — passed.

target.title: Add 1Password SecretRef plugin
target.body:
## Summary

- Adds a bundled `1password` plugin that provides a managed SecretRef exec provider for 1Password.
- Resolves SecretRefs through the official 1Password CLI (`op`) using service account or Connect auth env, while keeping resolved secrets out of OpenClaw config.
- Adds `openclaw 1password status` and `openclaw 1password setup` helpers for local and server workflows.
- Documents direct-host and container runtime requirements, including the fact that the plugin is bundled but the `op` CLI remains a runtime dependency.

## Linked context

Companion to the bundled Vault SecretRef plugin work in #89255, adding the same plugin-managed SecretRef provider pattern for 1Password.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: OpenClaw can configure and use the bundled `1password` SecretRef provider to resolve model provider credentials from 1Password without storing plaintext provider keys in OpenClaw config.
- Real environment tested: local Podman OpenClaw container using the bundled `1password` extension, a mounted OpenClaw data volume, a maintainer-provided 1Password service account token, and default vault `openclaw`.
- Secret material handling: the service account token and resolved provider credentials were not printed. Status output reports only whether auth env is present.
- Exact setup behavior observed: the container image staged a Linux `op` binary from `docker.io/1password/op:2`, validated it with `2.34.1`, and started the Gateway with `CLAW_1PASSWORD_OP=/home/node/.openclaw/bin/op-wrapper`.
- Evidence after fix: the `onepassword` provider was configured as a plugin-managed exec provider; the runtime saw the `op` wrapper; service account auth was present; the default vault was set.

From local run:

```json
{
  "providerAlias": "onepassword",
  "provider": {
    "configured": true,
    "source": "exec",
    "pluginIntegration": {
      "pluginId": "1password",
      "integrationId": "onepassword"
    }
  },
  "opCommand": "/home/node/.openclaw/bin/op-wrapper",
  "opCommandAvailable": true,
  "authMode": "service-account",
  "hasServiceAccountToken": true,
  "hasConnectHost": false,
  "hasConnectToken": false,
  "defaultVault": "openclaw"
}
```
and 

```
$ openclaw secrets audit --allow-exec
│
◇

OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (unknown) — Hot reload for config, cold sweat for deploys.

Secrets audit: findings. plaintext=1, unresolved=0, shadowed=0, legacy=0.
- [PLAINTEXT_FOUND] /home/node/.openclaw/openclaw.json:gateway.auth.token gateway.auth.token is stored as plaintext.
```

- Proof limitations or environment constraints: this proof used local Podman deployment. The `op` binary is intentionally not bundled into the plugin package; direct users and custom container images must provide a compatible 1Password CLI in the Gateway runtime.

## Tests and validation

Commands run locally:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/1password/src/cli.test.ts extensions/1password/index.test.ts extensions/1password/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:extensions
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/1password
pnpm plugins:inventory:check
node --check extensions/1password/onepassword-secret-ref-resolver.js
git diff --check
```

CLI smoke checks:


target.body:
Closes #104469

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tool schemas containing non-finite numeric values could be projected into provider-facing schemas with those values silently changed to `null`.

The trigger is a runtime/custom tool schema that contains a JavaScript-only numeric value such as `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` or `Number.NaN` in a JSON Schema numeric constraint/default. The shared projector serialized the schema with `JSON.stringify()` before validating the projected JSON value, so those values could become explicit `null` fields while reporting no schema violation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runtime tool schema projector now detects non-finite numbers before JSON serialization and reports the exact offending schema path as non-JSON-serializable.

This keeps the existing quarantine behavior narrow: the invalid tool is dropped with diagnostics, healthy sibling tools remain available, and provider-specific schema cleanup is left unchanged. The changed shared path is used by OpenAI and Anthropic tool projection; sibling provider paths such as Google/Gemini and Mistral use separate schema handling and are not changed by this PR.

## User Impact

Plugin/tool authors and operators get safer tool schema handling. Invalid non-finite numeric schema values now produce a clear projection violation instead of being silently rewritten into materially different provider payloads.

For example, a bad `bad_limits` tool with `maximum: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` is quarantined, while a healthy sibling `lookup` tool remains available for provider use.

target.title: fix(cli,doctor): use own-property checks for config field lookups
target.body:
### What Problem This Solves

CLI capability and doctor migration code uses `"apiKey" in <configObj>` to check whether credential ApiKey fields are present. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so an inherited property (e.g. via `Object.create({apiKey: "injected"})`) could be mistaken for an explicit user credential entry.

This is the **pre-Zod validation boundary** — the raw POJO config object from `JSON.parse()` before schema validation. These `in` checks operate on the raw object where prototype-chain properties from a crafted `__proto__` survive until the `Object.hasOwn()` gate.

### Why This Change Was Made

Use `Object.hasOwn()` which only checks own properties — inherited prototype properties are ignored. Config objects are plain POJOs from JSON, so `Object.hasOwn()` behaves identically for all legitimate config shapes while closing the prototype-chain attack surface.

### User Impact

No user-visible change for normal config. Prototype-chain inherited properties are no longer treated as explicit credential entries in TTS provider config detection and legacy web-search migration detection.

### Evidence

**Exact head**: `c0e64cd1d2c27468acaed324ddb79786db5e37f5f`

**Unit tests**:
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.own-entries.test.ts` — 4 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.test.ts` — 6 tests passed (existing)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` — 109 tests passed (existing)

**Runtime proof** (vitest + module-level integration):

```
-- 1/3. Core semantic proof — apiKey field --
  'apiKey' in Object.create({apiKey:"injected"}):     true
  Object.hasOwn(Object.create({apiKey:"injected"})):  false
  'apiKey' in {apiKey:"my-key"}:                       true
  Object.hasOwn({apiKey:"my-key"}):                    true
  'apiKey' in {}:                                      false
  ✓ Object.hasOwn() rejects proto, accepts own

-- 2/3. Real module test (legacy-web-search-migrate) --
  ✓ Proto-inherited apiKey NOT detected as legacy config path
  ✓ Own apiKey correctly detected as legacy config path

-- 3/3. Contract verification --

  ✓ src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts:listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths(apiKey) — SAFE

CONTRACT VERIFICATION:
  in operator:         ALL proto fields detected -> WOULD OVERRIDE
  Object.hasOwn():     ALL proto fields ignored -> SAFE
  Own properties:      both paths accept -> BACKWARD COMPAT
```

### Replacements

| `src/cli/capability-cli.ts` | `ttsProviderConfigHasApiKey` | `apiKey` |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-web-search-migrate.ts` | `listLegacyWebSearchConfigPaths` | `apiKey` |

Fixes an issue where Google Chat webhook authentication could hang indefinitely when Google's signing-certificate endpoint accepts a connection but never completes the HTTP response.

This path runs on cold start and again every 10 minutes when the cert cache expires, so a stalled `googleapis.com` request blocks all incoming Google Chat message verification until the gateway process is restarted.

Outbound Google Chat API timeouts were already addressed in #102227; this PR closes the remaining unbounded fetch in the inbound auth path. Related but distinct from #103627, which bounds the shared Gaxios Google-auth transport rather than this direct webhook certificate fetch.

Related: #5126

`fetchChatCerts()` in `extensions/googlechat/src/auth.ts` called `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a deadline. The fix adds a 30-second `timeoutMs` via a local `GOOGLECHAT_AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS` constant, matching the deadline already used for outbound Chat API calls and sibling channel auth paths.

No config/env knobs were added. The shared Gaxios transport timeout remains separate complementary work (#103627).

## User Impact

**Before:** A stalled cert endpoint leaves webhook auth pending forever; incoming Google Chat messages fail silently with no timeout error and no lane release.

**After:** Cert fetch aborts after 30 seconds with a concrete error; verification returns `{ ok: false, reason: ... }` and the gateway can continue processing other traffic.

- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Deadline matches outbound Google Chat API timeout and sibling auth control-plane paths (30s). Does not change Gaxios Google-auth transport (#103627) or outbound Chat control/media (#102227).

target.title: fix(config): reject zero-value cron.sessionRetention to prevent silent data loss
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Configuring `cron.sessionRetention: "0h"` (or any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to zero) is silently accepted by Zod config validation. `parseDurationMs("0h")` returns `0` without throwing, so the `superRefine` passes the value. `resolveRetentionMs` returns `0ms` with no guard, and `sweepCronRunSessions` computes `cutoff = now - 0 = now`, matching all cron run sessions for immediate deletion.

## Changes

**Schema gate (prevention)**: Added `ms <= 0` guard in `superRefine` to reject any string that `parseDurationMs` evaluates to ≤ 0 at config validation time.

**Doctor migration (upgrade safety)**: Added a registered legacy rule + migration that uses `parseDurationMs` (same `{ defaultUnit: "h" }` options as schema) in both detection and repair paths. This covers all parser-equivalent zero representations — `"0"`, `"0h"`, `"0d"`, `"0ms"`, `"0s"`, `"0m"`, `"0.0h"`, `"0h0m"`, `"0h0m0s"`, etc. The migration removes only values that parse to ≤ 0 so the documented 24h default applies; positive durations, `false`, and unparseable strings are preserved.

### Files changed (5 files, +230/-3)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.ts` | +11/-3: reject zero-duration in superRefine |
| `src/config/schema.test.ts` | +12: schema regression cases |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.cron.ts` | +68: parser-backed rule + migration spec |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.cron.test.ts` | +134: 16 focused tests |
| `src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.ts` | +2: register cron migration |

## Evidence

### All tests passing

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.cron.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.test.ts
Tests  60 passed (60)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.migrations.test.ts
Tests  63 passed (63)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.test.ts
Tests  6 passed (6)
```

### Doctor detection → repair → validation (bare number "0")

```
$ echo '{"agents":{"list":[{"id":"main"}]},"cron":{"sessionRetention":"0"}}' > /tmp/zero-num.json5
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/zero-num.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw doctor --fix --yes
```

Doctor detects via parser-backed rule:

```
Legacy config keys detected:
- cron: cron.sessionRetention is a zero duration — this causes
  immediate deletion of all cron run sessions. Run "openclaw doctor
  --fix" to remove it so the documented 24h default applies.
```

Doctor repairs:

```
Doctor changes:
Removed cron.sessionRetention "0" (zero duration); documented 24h
default applies.
```

After fix — `sessionRetention` removed, validation passes:

```
$ cat /tmp/zero-num.json5 | jq .cron
{"maxConcurrentRuns": 8}

$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/zero-num.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/zero-num.json5","warnings":[]}
```

### Before fix: schema gate rejects zero values

```
$ OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/cfg-zero.json5 pnpm --silent openclaw config validate --json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [{
    "path": "cron.sessionRetention",
    "message": "duration must be positive (use ms, s, m, h, d), e.g. 24h"
  }]
}
```

### Unparseable values preserved for schema diagnostic

`"abc"`, `""` — not matched by doctor rule, not removed by migration. Schema diagnostic handles these.

### Diff whitespace checks

`git diff --check` passed.

- **Not tested / proof gaps**: None.

target.title: fix(memory-core): guard catch-block async calls and supplement search against unhandled rejections
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Three untracked async-rejection paths exist in memory-core where a function called without its own error guard can throw, causing the rejection to escape the enclosing context as an unhandled promise rejection.

### 1. `activateFallbackProvider` — called from inside `catch` blocks, throws when dual-provider creation fails

Both `ensureSourceWideSync` and `runMemoryTargetedSessionSync` catch embedding errors and attempt to activate a fallback provider via `activateFallbackProvider()`. Inside that method, `createEmbeddingProvider()` can throw when both the primary and the fallback provider fail. Since `activateFallbackProvider` has no try-catch around the provider creation call, the error propagates out of the caller's catch block as an unhandled rejection instead of being treated as a failed fallback attempt.

### 2. `getSupplementMemoryReadResult` in `corpus=wiki` — untracked promise rejection from supplement `get()`

The `memory_get` tool's `corpus=wiki` branch calls `getSupplementMemoryReadResult()` without any try-catch. Previously failures could be reported as indistinguishable "not found"; now the actual backend error is surfaced.

### 3. `searchMemoryCorpusSupplements` — supplement search discarded all results when one failed

If any single supplement's `search()` throws, results from healthy supplements were discarded. Additionally, when ALL registered supplements fail, the error is now propagated so unavailable-phase handling returns an explicit unavailable result instead of silently reporting empty success.

## Changes

- `manager-sync-ops.ts`: `.catch()` on `createEmbeddingProvider` in `activateFallbackProvider` → returns `false` on failure instead of throwing
- `tools.ts corpus=wiki`: try-catch with `formatErrorMessage()` → surfaces actual backend failure, not "not found"
- `tools.shared.ts searchMemoryCorpusSupplements`: per-supplement try-catch with failure-count → isolates broken supplements; throws on all-fail for unavailable signal

## Evidence

**TypeScript:** clean on all changed files.

**Unit tests (26/26 passed):**

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)
```

### Gateway live proof (P1)

Isolated local Gateway + `memory-core` + `memory-wiki` environment. Plugins loaded: `memory-core`, `memory-wiki`, `proof-broken-corpus` (search throws), plus workspace memory seed.

```
host: <local-macOS>
date: 2026-07-11T13:25:07Z
gateway: ws://127.0.0.1:19001 (loopback, token auth)
state: <PROOF_STATE_DIR>
wiki vault: <PROOF_STATE_DIR>/wiki (seed page id: source.alpha)
```

**P1-A — `memory_search corpus=all` (one failing + one healthy supplement):**

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_search","args":{"query":"alpha","corpus":"all"},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_search",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "results": [
        {
          "corpus": "wiki",
          "path": "sources/alpha.md",
          "title": "Alpha",
          "kind": "source",
          "id": "source.alpha"
        },
        {
          "corpus": "memory",
          "path": "MEMORY.md",
          "startLine": 1,
          "endLine": 7,
          "citation": "MEMORY.md#L1-L7"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

Healthy wiki supplement result preserved while `proof-broken-corpus` search failure is isolated (no all-fail unavailable).

**P1-B — `memory_get corpus=wiki` (healthy wiki supplement):**

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_get","args":{"path":"source.alpha","corpus":"wiki","from":1,"lines":15},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_get",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "corpus": "wiki",
      "path": "sources/alpha.md",
      "title": "Alpha",
      "kind": "source",
      "id": "source.alpha",
      "fromLine": 1,
      "lineCount": 15,
      "truncated": true,
      "text": "\n# Alpha\n\n## Source\n- Type: `local-file`\n..."
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

**P1-C — `memory_get corpus=wiki` (supplement backend throws):**

Config: wiki disabled; external plugin `proof-broken-get` registers a corpus supplement whose `get()` throws.

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_get","args":{"path":"source.alpha","corpus":"wiki"},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_get",
  "output": {
    "details": {
      "path": "source.alpha",
      "text": "",
      "disabled": true,
      "error": "proof-broken-get corpus get failed"
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

Backend failure surfaced via `formatErrorMessage()` path; not reported as a generic healthy empty read.

**Summary of changes by file:**

| File | Change | Lines |
|------|--------|-------|
| `manager-sync-ops.ts` | `.catch()` on `createEmbeddingProvider` | +6/-0 |
| `tools.ts` | try-catch wiki get, surfaces actual error | +6/-1 |
| `tools.shared.ts` | per-supplement try-catch + failure-count, throws on all-fail | +8/-0 |
| `tools.citations.test.ts` | 3 proof tests | +99/-0 |

target.title: fix(outbound): preserve inline formatting on attributed b/i/s tags
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves `sanitizeForPlainText` in `src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.ts` converts inline HTML tags to channel-friendly lightweight markup. The current regexes for ``/``, ``/``, and ``/``/`` only match bare opening tags, so model output such as `bold` falls through to the generic tag stripper and arrives as plain text instead of `*bold*`. This is a sibling gap to #104118, which fixes the same issue for `` tags with attributes. ## Why This Change Was Made Updated the inline-formatting regexes to accept optional attributes on the opening tag (`/<(b|strong)(?:\s[^>]*)?>(.*?)<\/\1>/gi`, and likewise for `i/em` and `s/strike/del`), matching the existing pattern used for `]*>` and `]*>` and the `` fix in #104118. Added focused regression tests covering `class`, `style`, `id`, and data attributes. ## User Impact Users on channels that rely on `sanitizeForPlainText` (Telegram, iMessage, IRC, Google Chat, WhatsApp, etc.) will now see bold, italic, and strikethrough formatting preserved when models emit attributed inline tags, instead of silently stripped tags. ## Evidence - Added a regression test in `src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts` that asserts attributed ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, and `` tags are converted to `*`, `_`, and `~` wrapping respectively. - Local verification on head `095541f6e5`: - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts` → 29 passed - `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` → 0 errors - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.ts src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts` → exit code 0 ## Real behavior proof I ran a standalone script against the actual `sanitizeForPlainText` export on this PR's head (`095541f6e5`). It imports the current implementation and compares it with the old regex set (without the `(?:\s[^>]*)?` allowance) on attributed inline tags: ``` === outbound inline-tag attribute handling === bold input: bold before: bold after: *bold* strong input: bold before: bold after: *bold* italic input: italic before: italic after: _italic_ emphasis input: italic before: italic after: _italic_ strikethrough-s input: deleted before: deleted after: ~deleted~ strikethrough-strike input: old before: old after: ~old~ strikethrough-del input: removed before: removed after: ~removed~ === mixed content === input: Hello world and nice day before: Hello world and nice day after: Hello *world* and _nice_ ~day~ ``` Before the fix, attributed inline tags were stripped to plain text; after the fix, they are converted to the expected WhatsApp/Signal-style `*bold*`, `_italic_`, and `~strikethrough~` markers.

target.title: fix(feishu): avoid logging raw duplicate card-action tokens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where duplicate Feishu card-action callbacks could write the raw provider callback token into runtime diagnostics when the same callback token was received again inside the account-scoped dedupe window.

The callback token is still used internally as the dedupe key, but the operator-facing duplicate diagnostic no longer echoes that raw provider value back into logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Duplicate card-action handling now keeps the existing replay suppression behavior while changing only the duplicate diagnostic text. A repeated callback still produces a useful operational signal, but the log line no longer contains provider callback token material.

This does not change Feishu webhook authentication, callback parsing, card-action dispatch, retry handling, synthetic message routing, or the dedupe key used internally.

## User Impact

Operators can still see when duplicate Feishu card-action callbacks are skipped, without logs containing the raw callback token from the provider event.

AI-assisted.

## Evidence

### Redacted runtime-level duplicate callback transcript

The focused regression test replays the same Feishu card-action callback through `handleFeishuCardAction` twice with a captured runtime logger. This exercises the duplicate branch that the live Feishu event path reaches after `monitor.account.ts` parses `card.action.trigger` and passes `event.token` into the handler.

```text
callback token supplied by event: <redacted: non-empty provider callback token>
first handleFeishuCardAction(...) call: dispatches the quick action once
second handleFeishuCardAction(...) call with same token/account: duplicate is skipped
captured duplicate diagnostic: feishu[test-account]: skipping duplicate card action token
raw callback token present in captured logs: no
```

I could not produce a live Feishu workspace transcript from this machine because no live Feishu webhook/workspace credentials are configured here. The runtime-level replay above is the closest available behavior proof without disclosing or requiring a real tenant secret.

### Local validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot.card-action.test.ts` - passed, 23 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/bot.card-action.test.ts -t "does not log raw duplicate callback tokens"` - passed, focused duplicate-token regression
- `rg -n -F -- 'skipping duplicate card action token ${event.token}' extensions/feishu/src` - no matches
- `rg -n -F -- 'card action token ${' extensions/feishu/src` - no matches
- `git diff --check` - passed

### Remote CI note

Most PR checks passed on the current head. The remaining `checks-node-compact-large-3` failure is in `src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts`, outside the Feishu extension files changed by this PR. The `Real behavior proof` check previously failed because the PR body needed an authored problem/evidence section; this body update removes the invisible leading BOM and keeps both required sections visible to the checker.

target.title: fix(github-copilot): bound Copilot token exchange fetch timeout
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where GitHub Copilot API token exchange could hang forever after a cache miss when `api.<domain>/copilot_internal/v2/token` stopped responding.

`resolveCopilotApiToken()` in `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts` issued a bare `fetch` with no `AbortSignal` / timeout. Callers across model auth, embeddings, media understanding, and simple-completion refresh all reuse this helper, so a stalled exchange left those surfaces waiting indefinitely.

Sibling paths already had deadlines:

- GitHub Copilot device-code / token-poll OAuth uses `AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)`
- Copilot embedding `/models` discovery timeout is covered by open PR #102886

This PR covers the remaining exchange path itself.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a fixed internal 30-second per-request deadline via `AbortSignal.timeout` on the Copilot token-exchange fetch, aligned with `COPILOT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` in the Copilot OAuth helper. Map `AbortError` / `TimeoutError` to:

`Copilot token exchange timed out after 30000ms`

Preserve the original abort cause with `{ cause: error }`. The published `resolveCopilotApiToken` signature is unchanged — no public `timeoutMs` override.

## User Impact

**Before:** After Copilot token cache miss/expiry, a hung GitHub token-exchange endpoint could block Copilot model/embedding/auth refresh forever.

**After:** The exchange aborts at 30s with an explicit timeout error instead of hanging.

## Evidence

- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts` — fixed internal `AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)` on `resolveCopilotApiToken` exchange fetch; timeout errors preserve `{ cause }`
- Regression: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts`
  - success path asserts the exchange request carries an `AbortSignal`
  - hung mocked fetch aborts with the 30s timeout message
  - real `node:http` loopback that accepts TCP but never writes headers aborts via transport `fetchImpl` race (~250ms) while production still installs the 30s signal

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Copilot token exchange no longer leaves the GitHub `copilot_internal/v2/token` HTTP request unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return.
- **Canonical reachability path:**

```text
cache miss / expired github-copilot.token.json
  → resolveCopilotApiToken (plugin-sdk/provider-auth)
  → GET api.<domain>/copilot_internal/v2/token
  → AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)
  → TimeoutError → "Copilot token exchange timed out after 30000ms"
```

Callers that hit this helper include `extensions/github-copilot` token/models/embeddings paths, `src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.ts`, and `src/media-understanding/image.ts`.

- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production `resolveCopilotApiToken` exercised against a real Node HTTP server that accepts the connection and never sends response bytes (no live GitHub credential / blackhole required).
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Timeout value matches sibling Copilot OAuth request timeout (`30_000`). Published Plugin SDK signature unchanged (no `timeoutMs` param). Does not change device-code login or embedding `/models` discovery (the latter is #102886).
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node v22.22.0, branch `fix/copilot-token-exchange-timeout`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts -t "aborts hung Copilot token exchange|plus-signed Copilot token" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ accepts plus-signed Copilot token expiry strings 860ms
 ✓ aborts hung Copilot token exchange instead of waiting forever 1018ms
 ✓ aborts hung Copilot token exchange over HTTP transport 797ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed | 19 skipped (22)
 Duration  23.07s
```

- **Observed result after fix:**
  - Happy-path exchange request includes an `AbortSignal`
  - Mock hung fetch rejects with `Copilot token exchange timed out after 30000ms`
  - Real loopback hang (TCP accept, no headers) rejects with `Copilot token exchange timed out after 30000ms` in ~797ms wall time, proving undici/`fetch` honors abort on a live socket while the published helper keeps the fixed 30s deadline
- **What was not tested:** Live `api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token` blackhole with a real GitHub OAuth token; post-header body stalls after headers return.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes

target.title: Fix/OpenAI device code request timeout
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running OpenAI Codex device-code login (`openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code`, or the equivalent configure/wizard auth choice) could hang forever when a single `auth.openai.com` HTTP request stopped responding.

Before this patch, the flow only enforced a 15-minute poll-loop deadline around authorization waiting. The three `fetch` calls for user-code request, authorization poll, and token exchange had no per-request `AbortSignal` timeout, so a stalled TCP/proxy/blackhole response could bypass that deadline and leave the CLI spinner stuck. A server that returned headers and then stalled the body could also escape an incomplete timeout catch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat each device-code HTTP call as one timed operation: headers fetch plus bounded body read under the same `AbortSignal.timeout` (30s, aligned with the sibling ChatGPT browser OAuth token request timeout). Poll requests clamp that timeout to the remaining 15-minute authorization deadline and retry on per-operation timeout (including post-header body stalls) until the overall deadline expires. User-code and token-exchange timeouts fail fast with a clear error.

Scope stays OpenAI Codex device-code login HTTP only; browser OAuth and other providers are unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung device-code HTTP request (or a post-header body stall) could block `models auth login --device-code` indefinitely, even past the advertised 15-minute authorization window.

**After:** Each device-code request+body read aborts after 30 seconds (or sooner near the overall deadline). Poll timeouts retry within the 15-minute window; user-code and token-exchange stalls surface an explicit timeout error instead of hanging forever.

## Evidence

- `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.ts` — one operation deadline for fetch + body read on user-code, poll, and token-exchange; poll retries on timeout within the 15-minute deadline
- Regression: `extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts`
  - hung user-code aborts with timeout error
  - poll retries after `TimeoutError` and completes
  - hung token exchange aborts with timeout error
  - success path asserts all three fetches carry an `AbortSignal`
  - real `node:http` partial-body stall: user-code / token-exchange abort with formatted timeout; poll retries and succeeds

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** OpenAI Codex device-code login no longer leaves individual HTTP operations unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding before headers return, or returns headers and then stalls the body.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs device-code auth → `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `requestOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `pollOpenAICodexDeviceCode` / `exchangeOpenAICodexDeviceCode` → `runOpenAICodexDeviceCodeRequest` (`fetch` + `readOpenAICodexDeviceBody` under `AbortSignal.timeout(...)`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production device-code helpers exercised via colocated Vitest against a real hanging `node:http` loopback that sends headers then a partial JSON prefix and never finishes the body. Only `AbortSignal.timeout` duration is shortened for deterministic proof; the production fetch+body composition and error/retry mapping stay unmocked.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Matches the existing 30s OpenAI ChatGPT OAuth token request timeout; uses `AbortSignal.timeout` like GitHub Copilot device-flow request timeouts. Does not migrate this path onto `fetchWithSsrFGuard` in this change.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, product checkout on branch `fix/openai-device-code-request-timeout`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```
 ✓ aborts hung user-code requests instead of waiting forever 1ms
 ✓ retries device authorization polls after a per-request timeout 0ms
 ✓ aborts hung token exchange requests instead of waiting forever 0ms
 ✓ aborts when user-code headers arrive but the body never completes 31ms
 ✓ retries authorization polls after a post-header body stall 43ms
 ✓ aborts when token-exchange headers arrive but the body never completes 43ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
 Duration  1.37s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.53s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Hung user-code and token-exchange fetches abort with `OpenAI device code ... timed out after 30000ms`; a poll `TimeoutError` (including post-header body stall) is retried and the login can still succeed within the overall deadline. Real loopback partial-body stalls exercise production body consumption under the same operation signal.
- **What was not tested:** Live `openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code` against a real stalled `auth.openai.com` endpoint.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
